title: Problem Definition and Options Analysis
summary: How to establish whether there is a genuine market failure or harm that justifies intervention, gather the evidence, and compare regulatory and non-regulatory options.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to establish whether there is a genuine market failure or harm that justifies intervention, gather the evidence, and compare regulatory and non-regulatory options.
Learning Objectives: Define a regulatory problem in terms of harm, cause and scale
Gather and assess evidence to support the case for intervention
Compare options, including non-regulatory and do-nothing alternatives
Syllabus: Market failures, consumer harm and systemic risk as rationales
Evidence sources: supervisory data, complaints, research and surveys
Option sets: rules, guidance, disclosure, supervision or no action
Exercise: writing a problem statement and options paper
Intended Audience: Policy and rule-making staff developing rules, guidance and policy positions
Legal advisers and drafters working on secondary rules and supervisory guidance
Supervisors and economists who contribute evidence, impact analysis or consultation input
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of policy, legal or supervisory work is helpful. No formal legal or economics training is required.
Core Reading: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Regulatory Policy and Governance (2012)
OECD, Best Practice Principles for Regulatory Policy: Regulatory Impact Assessment (2020)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
